item.title: UConn women's basketball: Here's what we learned from three preseason wins
item.description: UCONN players cheer on their team in the second half against Army at the M&T Bank Center at Gampel Pavilion in Storrs on October 25, 2026. (Arnold Gold/Hearst Connecticut Media) UConn women's basketball begins the regular season next Monday. The curtain rises in Hartford on the 2026-27 season, and the Huskies once again begin their quest for glory. A 26 th Final Four appearance and a 13 th national championship are the goal. Geno Auriemma begins his 42 nd year at the helm with a roster that boasts the reigning national player of the year. But before it all begins, before it all counts, Auriemma has a few days left of preseason practice to fine-tune his squad. The No. 2 Huskies won three preseason exhibitions, including a win over Texas, which has reached the Final Four in back-to-back years. In those wins, UConn introduced two freshmen while Sarah Strong showcased her leadership and the Huskies proved their defense will be the pillar of their identity. Auriemma also saw some growing pains. The Huskies' offense needs involvement, their post players lacks consistency, and they still have three players out due to injury. "When it's good, I like it. There's a lot of good things, and then there's a lot of things that get in the way of us being good," he said Sunday after UConn's 86-50 exhibition win over Army. "I don't know that we're set yet on the lineup that works best. So, we'll continue to work on that. But we played three games, so that's good, and now I think everybody's ready for the next phase. "We're not there yet, but we're not supposed to be there yet. It's still early in the season." UCONN coaches from left, Chris Dailey, Geno Auriemma and Morgan Valley watch UCONN defeat Army at the M&T Bank Center at Gampel Pavilion in Storrs on October 25, 2026. (Arnold Gold/Hearst Connecticut Media) UConn opens the season hosting Cornell. Three days later, it faces its first test of the season when it travels to Ann Arbor to face No. 5 Michigan. The November slate continues with matchups against No. 10 Iowa, No. 18 Ohio State, No. 7 Louisville, No. 1 South Carolina and No. 4 Duke. The first month of the season will be the Huskies' hardest. In December, they also have dates with No. 20 Maryland, No. 13 Notre Dame and No. 9 LSU. How the Huskies survive their November gauntlet will determine how they approach the rest of their non-conference. With such a front-loaded schedule, Auriemma will weigh what he saw in the preseason differently. Will his newcomers be ready for early challenges? Is the team's defensive chemistry strong enough? Will Blanca Quiñonez, the 2026 Big East Freshman and Sixth Woman of the Year, be available? "I think we're pretty ready," said redshirt junior Jana El Alfy. "I think it's a little different than what we had last year, and having a couple of (preseason) games to start a little earlier is going to help us prepare early and have us ready earlier." item.title: Nuggets reportedly interested in $10M streaky combo guard to pair with Nikola Jokic, Jamal Murray
item.description: Nuggets reportedly interested in $10M streaky combo guard to pair with Nikola Jokic, Jamal Murray originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Denver Nuggets are off to a somewhat sloppy start, which isn't necessarily a bad thing this early in the season as they work to figure things out. The team had limited options this offseason, as its salary cap situation made significant moves difficult. Denver has had some rough outings, including its win over the New Orleans Pelicans , when the team found itself trailing by a significant margin. After the game, Nikola Jokic went off on fans who booed the team. “I think the fans that booed us are not welcome here anymore, if you ask me… if you guys follow us, you know that we never quit and we came back from much worse for similar situations,” Jokic said. Then, on Monday, the Nuggets suffered a convincing loss to the Golden State Warriors . In fact, Jokic didn't play during the final four minutes of the game, as the Warriors secured their first win of the season. “Nikola Jokić watched the final three and a half minutes of Monday night's matchup with the Golden State Warriors from the bench. Denver Nuggets head coach David Adelman had pulled his starters after a Gui Santos 3-pointer gave the visitors a 21-point lead — the sort of deficit that not even a three-time NBA Most Valuable Player could erase, even if he and his teammates were playing at the peak of their powers,” Yahoo Sports’ Dan Devine wrote. Despite the slow start, Denver could be looking to make an addition to its roster. The Stein Line's Jake Fischer reported that the Nuggets have expressed interest in Kevin Porter Jr. “Yet several teams, sources say, are still evaluating their respective backcourts and could emerge as potential Porter suitors depending on how things unfold. Two such teams, according to sources, are Denver and Sacramento,” Fischer wrote. Acquiring Porter could be a good move for Denver, as he could provide streaky scoring off the bench. The Nuggets need to explore different options at this point, and bringing in a new face could be a good place to start. Porter is currently playing on a $10 million contract with the Milwaukee Bucks. While he wouldn't be the biggest addition Denver could make, bringing him in could be a smart move that pays dividends, particularly if the Nuggets eventually pursue more significant trades. item.title: Knicks' Mike Brown admits Karl-Anthony Towns, Jalen Brunson lineup experiment already failed
item.description: Knicks' Mike Brown admits Karl-Anthony Towns, Jalen Brunson lineup experiment already failed originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Knicks ' regular season last year wasn't the best by any means, but head coach Mike Brown had a purpose behind his approach. Brown used different lineups throughout the season to determine what worked and what didn't. When the postseason arrived, he knew which rotations to rely on in certain situations. It was a strategy that paid off after being implemented from the beginning of the regular season. “Brown was brought in partly to, and partly won a championship off, the willingness to use the regular season to experiment over trying to maximize wins. He installed a brand new offensive system, shortened starters’ minutes to save them for the rigors of the postseason, and constantly tried new players and lineups,” SNY’s David Vertsberger wrote. Brown has tried taking the same approach this season, but it hasn't worked as well early on. New York picked up its first win on Tuesday night, but after starting the season 0-3, Brown didn't hold back when discussing the team's struggles. “Our crap stinks. It does. And we're the only ones that can do something about it,” Brown said. The Knicks head coach has already experimented with something he didn't do much of last season. This time, it involved Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns. Brown wanted to try a different approach, but it didn't work as planned, as there were stretches when both stars were on the bench. “My big experimentation was playing KAT and Jalen in two stretches together. And so the middle of [the game], I had both KAT and Jalen off the floor. We didn’t really do that last year. Watching it, I think we did it in the preseason some, but we didn’t play everybody all the time so it was a little harder, but watching it, I didn’t like it,” Brown told the media. It's safe to say Brown will likely take that option off the table for the foreseeable future after seeing how it played out. Still, it was another lineup experiment that provided valuable information about what doesn't work for this team. New York needs Brunson and Towns on the court together as much as possible, and having both stars on the bench at the same time can disrupt the team's offensive flow. Now, Brown will have to look at other lineup combinations that could give the Knicks better results moving forward. item.title: Sergio Pérez's ‘Second Father’: The Man Behind Mexico's Motorsport Revival
item.description: Cadillac F1 driver Sergio Pérez spoke to the importance of Carlos Slim Domit and Escudería Telmex to motorsport in Mexico during the United States Grand Prix. (Photo credit: Greg Kallman / FanAmp) All eyes will be on Cadillac Formula 1 driver Sergio Pérez this weekend, because the Mexican driver's 300th career Grand Prix will take place at his home race, the Mexico City Grand Prix . And while many onlookers might pinpoint Checo's presence as the reason for the skyrocketing popularity of motorsport in the country, we can actually credit a different man for the feat: Carlos Slim Domit, who has been providing support to Latin American drivers through a program called Escudería Telmex. For Pérez, Carlos Slim Domit is a “second father.” For other drivers he sponsors, Slim is an idol who has become a friend and confidant. For Latin America, Slim has done more than almost anyone to grow motorsport’s audience, from televising races throughout the region to putting its drivers on the world stage. In order to truly gauge the impact of Escudería Telmex, I spoke to three drivers involved in the program: Sergio Pérez, Andrés Pérez de Lara, and Tatiana Calderón. All three drivers had nothing but praise for Slim; taken together, they paint a picture of a wealthy man who has used his fortune to raise the profile of racing throughout Latin America and abroad. Carlos Slim Domit: motorsport’s Mexican godfather Carlos Slim Domit has transformed motorsport in Mexico and around the world. (Photo credit: World Economic Forum via Wikimedia Commons) Born in Mexico City on February 28, 1967, Carlos Slim Domit is a Mexican businessman who hails from one of Mexico's most exceptional families. His father, Carlos Slim Helú, grew up in a wealthy family and began investing in various businesses after graduating from the National Autonomous University of Mexico with a degree in engineering. Those investments succeeded; however, he is most closely associated with two different telecommunications companies, Telmex and Telcel, that provide everything from landline phone service to internet access for folks all throughout Mexico. His investments there came just before the cell phone and internet booms, which then saw him amass even more wealth and eventually become Mexico's richest man. The billionaire's son, Carlos Slim Domit, took up the mantle in the business realm — but one of his driving passions is motorsport, which led to the creation of a groundbreaking team that has provided support to drivers in Spanish-speaking countries throughout the Americas. item.title: Will Nick Sirianni be coaching the Philadelphia Eagles next year?
item.description: The Philadelphia Eagles are in the midst of a nightmare season. They’re 2-5 and have lost five straight games. Their franchise QB, Jalen Hurts, is out for the season with blood clots, and running back Saquon Barkley can’t stay healthy. Their offense is riddled with injuries, and now they have to rely on backup QB Tanner McKee to lead their offense. There were high hopes for this talented roster, but it’s been a disaster since they won the first two games of the season. Drama always seems to surround head coach Nick Sirianni. Now people are asking if he is the right man for the job. MORE: Cowboys’ win over Eagles has not changed Troy Aikman’s opinion about Dallas Will the Eagles fire Nick Sirianni? Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni. Mandatory Credit: Matt Marton-Imagn Images There’s a ton of questions surrounding the Eagles, and Nick Sirianni’s future is one of them. The Super Bowl champ has faced criticism for his in-game decisions and how he handled questions about the team’s handling of Jalen Hurts’ blood clot situation. #Eagles HC Nick Sirianni got into a back-and-forth with a reporter over why Jalen Hurts was allowed to fly back from London after being diagnosed with a blood clot: https://t.co/OulKwe7Q8x pic.twitter.com/QqlEpCXhAc — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) October 19, 2026 Sirianni doesn’t call plays on either side of the ball and is never afraid to confront critics, including fans. The Eagles probably won’t make the playoffs this season, so the Philly brass will have plenty of time to evaluate Sirianni’s job. The 45-year-old has a career 61-30 record and a Super Bowl championship to his name. A big test comes in Week 8 with a Sunday Night Football tilt against NFC East rival, the Washington Commanders . If they get embarrassed in a primetime game, major changes could follow. Nick Foles said yesterday that there is "dysfunction in Philly," questioning the Eagles' culture. Joe DeCamara asked Nick Sirianni about Foles' comments today: "Nick Foles isn't in the building with us." pic.twitter.com/3cwlPpSBur — SPORTSRADIO 94WIP (@SportsRadioWIP) October 28, 2026 Even if the Eagles fire Sirianni, is the job attractive? Hurts’ health is uncertain, Barkley is aging, and you never know what you’ll get from their defense. GM Howie Roseman never shies away from a big swing, so a new coach would at least know his GM wants to win football games. This squad faces a ton of “what if?” questions right now. Will Siranni be around when those questions are answered? He likely won’t be if losses and drama keep piling up. item.title: Liverpool Starting XI vs Chelsea: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup
item.description: Liverpool Starting XI vs Chelsea: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup Liverpool vs Chelsea: Predicted XI, Team News and Andoni Iraola’s Carabao Cup Dilemma Andoni Iraola has a straightforward problem, the kind coaches usually prefer. Liverpool are winning, confidence is high and the squad has options. The complication is that Chelsea arrive at Anfield in the Carabao Cup with enough attacking quality to punish sentiment, fatigue or over-rotation. Liverpool come into the tie after a 2-0 win over Brighton, a result that brought points and momentum, but also demanded plenty physically. That matters. Cup selection is rarely about rewarding the last performance, it is about managing the next one. IMAGO Liverpool team news before Chelsea clash Iraola rotated in the previous round without throwing the competition away. Lewis Koumas, Rio Ngumoha, Trey Nyoni and James McConnell all started as Liverpool beat Tottenham Hotspur 3-1, while senior players were still used to give the side enough authority. This time, the balancing act looks tighter. Florian Wirtz is believed to be fit after going off with a knock against Brighton, but there is little sense in taking an unnecessary risk in October. Dominik Szoboszlai and Victor Munoz are still recovering, which reduces Liverpool’s creative depth if Wirtz does not start. That leaves Alexander Isak as the obvious constant. He has six goals in seven Premier League appearances and Liverpool would be taking something important out of the side if they rested him as well. Bradley Barcola could retain his place, while Ngumoha looks a credible option again on the right. Predicted Liverpool XI for Carabao Cup tie If Wirtz is left out, Nyoni may be pushed into a more advanced role, with Alexis Mac Allister and Ryan Gravenberch behind him. That midfield would give Liverpool control and enough security against Chelsea’s forward runners. At the back, the problem is specific. Jeremie Frimpong and Conor Bradley remain unavailable, so right-back is still awkward. Joe Gomez and Ronald Araujo are both possibilities there, though Iraola may decide Chelsea are too dangerous to experiment too much with the defensive unit. Milos Kerkez has the legs to go again at left-back, and the partnership between Virgil van Dijk and Jérémy Jacquet has started to settle. In goal, Giorgi Mamardashvili is expected to continue the cup rotation. Predicted Liverpool XI: Mamardashvili, Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Kerkez, Mac Allister, Gravenberch, Ngumoha, Nyoni, Barcola, Isak Selection call could define Liverpool approach This is where Iraola earns his money. Go too strong and you risk wear and tear. Rotate too heavily and Chelsea take control of the night. The most likely answer is a team that mixes freshness with authority, and that usually means keeping your best striker on the pitch and your structure intact. Injured: Bradley, Frimpong, Szoboszlai, Ekitike, Munoz. Kick-off is 8pm GMT on Wednesday, October 28, 2026 at Anfield.

Whitaker/San Antonio Express-News) SALT LAKE CITY -When the Spurs watched film of the season's first three games earlier this week, the need for defensive improvement was a big point of emphasis. But it wasn't the biggest one. While they spent substantial time exploring ways to start games stronger defensively after giving up 30-plus points in the first quarter of each outing, the Spurs' meatiest discussion focused on how to jump start All-Star center Victor Wembanyama after he averaged just 20.0 points on 36.5% shooting from the field and 25.0% accuracy from 3-point range. "We got to get Vic more involved," forward Devin Vassell said after practice Monday. "We talked about it in the film (session). Their study paid off Tuesday night when Wembanyama scored a season-high 29 points on 14 of 21 from the field in a 130-103 thrashing of lowly Sacramento at the Frost Bank Center. Although he went 0 of 3 from 3-point land, it didn't matter because he feasted in the paint, recording a career-best nine dunks after totaling only 10 in the first three games. The 7-foot-4 Frenchman's dominance down low started early with a pair of buckets on lob passes from De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle in the first 2:19. "We always try to do it, because (the dunk) is the most efficient shot in the game," said Wembanyama, who also had 10 rebounds and five blocks in 27 minutes. item.title: Real Madrid Apologizes For Mbappé ‘Dictator’ Comments—After Chinese Broadcasters Drop Games
item.description: Topline Real Madrid, the Spanish LaLiga soccer club and current home for Kylian Mbappé, apologized to the Chinese people on Wednesday one day after the French star forward referred to Mao Zedong as a “Chinese dictator” on a podcast—a comment that received intense backlash in the country. Chinese state broadcasters have reportedly stopped airing games featuring the star French player. Real Madrid via Getty Images Key Facts In a previous podcast interview, Mbappé said he liked a meme where fans superimposed his face on an image of Mao Zedong, the Chinese communist revolutionary leader who died in 1976, referring to him not by name but as a “Chinese dictator.” The comments received swift backlash in China, and prompted major companies to end sponsorship deals with the French soccer player. In a statement on Wednesday, Real Madrid apologized to the Chinese people for “any discomfort caused by the recent words of our player Kylian Mbappé,” and professed a “deep respect” for the country and its people. The statement came after broadcasters in China said they would now stop airing games or ads featuring Mbappé—China Central Television (CCTV) suspended LaLiga matches featuring the French star, ESPN reported, while broadcaster Migu said it would not air Real Madrid’s upcoming match on Sunday, Reuters reported. What Exactly Did Mbappé Say? Mbappé responded to a question about his favorite meme featuring himself during an interview with French podcast “The Bridge.” His answer was “a video someone made of a guy… I think he was a Chinese dictator.” Mbappé apologized quickly after several Chinese companies ended their sponsorship deals with him, including beverage giant Dongpeng and dairy companies Mengniu and Milkground. “I apologize to everyone my words have upset,” the Real Madrid forward said, adding “this was not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry.” How Has China Responded? “We take seriously the apology he has made,” Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said at a press briefing on Wednesday, the Associated Press reported. What to Watch For LaLiga and the league’s president Javier Tebas issued their own apologies on Tuesday, with Tebas insisting “we will implement concrete measures to help ensure that situations like this do not happen again.” It is currently unclear if the Chinese broadcasters will agree to resume airing Real Madrid games. On Wednesday, the president of the Spanish league said he met with China’s ambassador to Spain in order to “seek solutions to move past this episode.” This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.title: Making the case for and against the 49ers to go all in
item.description: At 7-1, the San Francisco 49ers are the favorites to win the Super Bowl this season, even after their first loss of the year, as they enter a needed bye week to get healthy. Coming out of that bye week, though, and looking towards the second half of the season, their team could look different. The 49ers already traded for defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, sending a fourth-round pick to the Indianapolis Colts for the 32-year-old on an expiring contract. And more could be coming, with the 49ers still having a few gaps to fill on their roster. Following the 7-1 start, many have looked for San Francisco to push all the chips in for a Super Bowl this season, which would involve sending serious capital for stars. The 49ers are no stranger to trade deadline moves, although some, most notably the Christian McCaffrey trade, have had more magnitude than others. Over the years, we’ve seen teams go all in and hurt themselves for the future, while others have taken the pieces they’ve acquired with them on a Super Bowl run. Does it make sense for San Francisco to go all in here? Let’s make the case for both sides. Why they should As I mentioned at the top, the 49ers are the clear favorites to win the Super Bowl currently, followed by the Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs, Seattle Seahawks, and Los Angeles Rams. We know the 49ers flaws, with injuries easily being the main issue. But when you look at the NFL, it’s easy to poke holes in nearly every contender. Buffalo’s defense has been a major question mark. Kansas City still doesn’t have those top-tier receiving threats, and their defense lost some key talent over the offseason. Seattle has struggled without Klint Kubiak at times offensively, and Sam Darnold has been erratic. And the Rams have just outright struggled on both sides of the ball at times. The field is quite wide open right now. And after all the failures and miscues with reaching and winning a Super Bowl in the last few years, this could be San Francisco’s shot to do it all. If they do win the trophy, there’s no worrying talk about going all in at all. San Francisco also has very few holes on its roster. Realistically, they could just push all their chips in on an edge rusher and call it a day. They could also go for rotational pieces that can be more complementary to their depth. item.description: Bountiful’s Braden Boucha fights to bring down Morgan’s George Thurston as they compete in a high school football game in Morgan on Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026. | Scott G Winterton, Deseret News 3A Quarterfinal Previews No. 9 Cedar (6-5) at No. 1 Morgan (8-2) 3A quarterfinals Friday, Oct. 30, 6 p.m. Parry’s Power Guide: Morgan by 23 All-time series: Cedar leads 2-1 since 2003 Last meeting: Cedar won 17-14 at Cedar (Oct. 28, 2006, 3A first round) What Cedar needs to do to win Cedar is the defending 3A champion, even if its record doesn’t look like it. Last year the Reds went 13-0 and beat Manti 41-35 for the first state title in school history. This season has been harder. In the middle of the year, Cedar lost three straight 3A South games to playoff teams: 38-7 at No. 5 seed Richfield, 19-9 at No. 6 seed Canyon View and 31-24 to No. 2 seed Juab. Since then the Reds have won 49-3 at Carbon and 44-20 at North Sanpete in the first round. That’s 93 points in two games. Cedar’s record is better than it looks. Two of its five losses came by a combined five points to 4A teams: 34-30 at Pine View and 35-34 to Dixie. The Reds also beat 4A Snow Canyon 10-6. Snow Canyon is the 4A No. 4 seed and a Region 9 co-champion. Cedar also beat 4A Wasatch 29-19 and 3A Manti 38-28. The offense starts with Braxton DeMille, who has 1,224 rushing yards and 15 touchdowns on 209 carries. Hunter Burgess is the team’s big-play threat. He has 49 catches for 1,072 yards and 11 touchdowns, averaging 21.9 yards per catch. He also leads the defense with five interceptions and has two return touchdowns, giving him 14 total touchdowns. Two quarterbacks share the job. Jackson Mann has thrown for 1,377 yards and 13 touchdowns with only three interceptions, and he’s run for 434 yards. Colt Kelling averages 22 yards per completion and has six touchdown passes. Cody Stevenson has made eight field goals and has 61 points. To pull off the upset, Cedar has to keep Morgan’s offense off the field with DeMille and protect the ball, which it has done well: Mann and Kelling have five interceptions combined. Cedar’s defense has 12 interceptions, and Morgan’s Owen Gilson has thrown 10. If the Reds can force a couple of turnovers and let Burgess make a big play or two, the defending champions can stay in the game. Tye Hiatt has done it before: two years ago Cedar was 4-7, and last year it went 13-0. What Morgan needs to do to win Morgan needs to keep playing the way it has all season. The Trojans lead 3A in scoring offense (41.7 ppg) and rank second in scoring defense (13.8 ppg) behind Richfield. item.title: Record breaking kite surfer finds 'magic gust'
item.description: Lewis Crathern, from Worthing, reached 42.6 metres (139.76 ft) during a stormy session at Bracklesham Bay [Eunice Bergin] An acclaimed kite surfer from West Sussex who recently made history with a record-breaking jump said he is "ecstatic that the record has come to the UK, to my home area". Lewis Crathern, from Worthing, reached 42.6m (139.76 ft) during a stormy session at Bracklesham Bay last Friday, after finding what he called "that magic gust". The jump, which was independently verified as a world record by the WOO sports platform, is another in a long list of career achievements for the 41-year-old. He said: "I have been doing this for 22 years, I grew up on the seafront in Worthing, I feel very comfortable in the stormy ocean." Crathern credited sponsor Harlem with giving him good equipment to manage the difficult conditions [Eunice Bergin] Crathern said he was able to make the stormy conditions work for him. "The bad weather in our sport becomes the good weather. You become the kite," he said. In the late 2010s, he completed challenges such as jumping over the Brighton and Worthing piers. But he says that a person does not need "an 18 year old's body" to do jumps like these, but "experience and the right mindset". The kite surfer said he would like to use this jump as a "platform" to drive the advocacy work he does with sponsor, Global Wind Energy Council. Crathern wants to inspire other people towards wind energy and renewables, and already works with young people to try and spread that message. As for the record, he said it was achieved by sheer dedication. "It's like being an airline pilot, the more hours you put in, the better you become," he added. item.title: Phil Vandersea of Northbridge, who played for NFL's first Super Bowl champion, dies at 84
item.description: A Northbridge native who was on the Green Bay Packers team that won the first Super Bowl in 1967 died Saturday, Oct. 24. Phil Vandersea, who starred for Northbridge High School and the University of Massachusetts at Amherst before playing for Vince Lombardi and the Packers, died at 84. He left behind his wife, Sandra, with whom he was married for 59 years; a son, Scott; a daughter, Kathy; and his grandchildren. Vandersea was born in Northbridge and played basketball and football for Northbridge High, graduating in 1961. From there he went to UMass, where he is recognized as one of the top players in program history. A fullback who also played linebacker and shared punting duties, Vandersea was a key player on the undefeated Minutemen team of 1963, running for 388 yards and six touchdowns for a team that won the Yankee Conference championship. Vandersea was named to the UMass All-Century team in 1982 and was inducted into its athletics hall of fame in 2012 . Vandersea was selected by the Packers in the 16th round of the 1965 NFL draft. As a rookie, he joined a formidable Packers team, led by coach Lombardi, that dominated the 1960s, winning five NFL championships in that decade, including the first two Super Bowls. "He was the kind of man that, if you were in a room, and he walked in, even if you didn’t see him, you knew he was there,” Vandersea said of Lombardi, in a 2016 interview with the T&G. “He was usually pretty stern, expecting the most and the best out of you. No one got any favors. It didn’t matter who you were, he’d scream at you just like anybody else." More: Northbridge High graduate Phil Vandersea made history with Packers in Super Bowl I Listed at 6 feet, 3 inches tall and 245 pounds, Vandersea showcased the versatility that he had earlier displayed at UMass, playing fullback, linebacker, tight end, defensive tackle and defensive end, as well as on special teams. Vandersea recalled being the only player from New England on the Packers, which stood out on a team mostly made up of players from the South and Midwest. "My teammates called me Funny Talker,” Vandersea said in the 2016 interview. “They were all from Florida, Texas or someplace in the South. They’d never heard anybody with a New England accent like mine." In his rookie season of 1966, the Packers defeated the Dallas Cowboys for the NFL championship. That victory qualified the Packers for the first-ever AFL-NFL World Championship Game, an experimental game created by NFL Commissioner Pete Rozelle to pit the NFL champion against the champion of the upstart American Football League. In what would later be dubbed Super Bowl I, Vandersea's Packers defeated the Kansas City Chiefs, 35-10 in front of 70 million viewers on television.
